text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for service `batch-scheduler` in us-west-2. threshold=5% over 5m. alert-id=ALRT-17965
alejandra: taking initial on-call lead, switching presence to incident mode. joining now
maya: oncall-sre joining the thread. will take secondary. please post any immediate mitigations here
jay: eng-runtime watching the scheduler logs. initial suspicion: batching window collapse -> head-of-line stall causing long enqueue delays and gateway timeouts
luke: support ops: we're seeing customer reports of timeouts (client-side 10s -> 502). CS queue filling, escalating to sales for impacted accounts
ana: PM - need impact numbers and ETA. which customers & how bad?
rahul: CustSuccess: 8 customers with active requests affected, 3 marked high-priority. notified account owners. customers asking for ETA and mitigation steps
maya: metrics snippet: `scheduler.enqueue_time_ms` median 12 -> 3200, backlog_size=4200, inflight_batches=480
jay: log sample: ```
2026-06-10T12:05:21Z ERROR gateway upstream=502 service=batch-scheduler region=us-west-2 queue_depth=4200 window_ms=2300
```
maya: seeing KV-cache prefetch spike and tokenizer workers thrashing — locks holding on batch assembly thread
alejandra: immediate mitigation plan: 1) route traffic to fallback smaller-batch variant 2) throttle non-enterprise ingress 3) evict stale queued requests >30s. executing now
ops-bot: Runbook invoked: step1 set fallback variant weight. Command: `rbctl route set-weight --service batch-scheduler --region us-west-2 --variant v1-small=1.0`
jay: applying route change (doing slow-weight switch) — watching for regression in 30s
alejandra: also enabling edge ingress throttle: reduce allowed concurrent non-enterprise QPS to 60%
maya: queued-eviction script running: `scripts/evict-old-queue.sh --service batch-scheduler --age 30` — evicted ~900 stale requests so far
luke: CS update: notification batch sent to impacted customers, ETA communicated ~15m. two customers requested priority callbacks
rahul: Dedicated customers: 2 of the impacted are on dedicated pools; they show degraded latency but not full failure. coordinating with dedicated infra owners
jay: after fallback weighting: p95 enqueue dropped from ~3s to ~180ms, 5xx rate down from 12% -> 3% in last 60s
maya: scheduling rolling restart of the routing-proxy in us-west-2 (5m maintenance window) to clear stuck connections and reset tokenizers
ana: PM note: capture timestamps for toggles and customer messages for postmortem and possible SLA credit decisions
alejandra: handing primary to SRE Maya for follow-up/RCAs. I'll stay available for coordination
maya: ack, taking lead. next actions: collect traces, heap/threads dumps for batch-assembler, reproduce locally with loadgen, check KV-prefetch config and backoff thresholds
jay: also deploying a canary that reduces tokenizer batch size (config: token_batch=8) to test performance/quality tradeoff
luke: CS: 1 customer confirmed mitigation resolved their issue. 2 are asking for written incident summary and possible credit
maya: saving artifacts to /infra/incidents/1796504321/artifacts (logs, graphs, traces). Will open a postmortem doc in #postmortems after triage
ops-bot: Reminder: if any customer requests credit, create ticket `INC-17965` in billing queue
alejandra: closing out on-call takeover. If 5xx creeps back up, re-open pager immediately. Good job team :thumbsup:
maya: will post timeline + RCA by EOD and assign owners for fix (adjust batching window heuristics, improve kv-prefetch backoff). handing off monitoring to eng-runtime Jay
incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 and page window extended +30m. Audit log updated.
